rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. Testing RNA-only with singleprofile and pca_n2000 isolates the effect of RNA encoding and profile settings, providing foundational performance metrics. This clarifies whether RNA-only models are viable before exploring multimodal or image-only approaches.

The existing evidence shows that rna_only with singleprofile and pca_n2000 achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration by extending the singleprofile baseline while keeping RNA encoder and image encoder consistent, providing critical insights into whether multiprofile or aggregation methods improve performance.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated model) in the multiprofile setting improves accuracy, isolating the impact of representation choice. This balances exploitation of the multiprofile advantage with exploration of encoder improvements, prioritizing a key design choice with potential for meaningful performance gains.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings (0.650 accuracy) with scvi_n200 RNA encoder outperform singleprofile and PCA-based models. This experiment tests whether adding image data (resnet50) to the scvi_n200 RNA encoder in a multimodal setup with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion can further improve accuracy. It isolates the effect of multimodal integration while leveraging the best-performing RNA encoder and profile setting, balancing exploration of image data's value with minimal changes to proven components.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile settings and scvi_n200 encoder (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6501). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (config_006) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of the promising RNA-only direction with exploration of a key design choice (aggregation), which could yield significant gains without overcomplicating the model.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.653). However, multimodal approaches with resnet50 (config_030) underperform. This experiment tests whether using weighted fusion (vs. concat in config_030) with the best RNA encoder (scvi_n200) and transformer aggregation could bridge this gap. It isolates the impact of fusion method while leveraging proven RNA and aggregation choices, balancing exploitation of strong RNA-only results with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_033) achieve high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a stronger vision transformer) further improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. This is critical for determining if the current top-performing configuration can be surpassed by a more advanced vision model, while maintaining the effective fusion strategy.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with imagenet_vit_l and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.7249). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt (a more advanced model) further improves performance while keeping other components (image encoder, aggregation, fusion) consistent. This clarifies the impact of the RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and could potentially push accuracy higher without overcomplicating the model.

The existing evidence shows config_039 (multimodal, scgpt, vit_l, transformer, weighted) has the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether using resnet50 instead of vit_l as the image encoder, while keeping other parameters the same, affects performance. It isolates the image encoder's impact, which is critical for understanding key contributors to accuracy. With one experiment left, this comparison helps determine if the image encoder choice is pivotal.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, and transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_039) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests a similar configuration with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion to isolate the impact of fusion method. It is the best use of the last experiment to validate if the fusion strategy is the key factor driving performance.
